move: four tiles fly in from four edges, layout reshuffles twice, snap out
how: Four rounded image tiles in a 2x2 grid fly in from four edges (x ∓700 or y ∓900 with ±6-8 rotation, expo.out 0.8s, 0.1s apart) while a masked headline rises, a footer line slides from x -30 and a pill pops with back.out(2). Four story-progress segments fill scaleX 0→1 linearly, one per second. Inside every tile the image drifts scale 1→1.08 and xPercent -2→2 linearly for the whole duration. At 37% the layout shifts by tweening left/top/width/height with expo.inOut over 0.9s: tile 1 grows to a 940x900 feature and tiles 2-4 line up as 296x370 thumbnails below (0.05s offsets); at 65% tile 2 takes the feature and tile 1 drops to the row. Exit at 86%: tiles snap to y -1400 with expo.in (stagger 0.05), headline exits upward, footer fades down.
adapt: Replace the four images and numbers, the headline, footer line and pill text, and the two feature layouts' pixel boxes; keep the 0.1s fly-in cadence and the 0.9s expo.inOut reflows at 1.5s and 2.6s.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the dots, header, four tiles and footer; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with fly-in 0.01-0.3D, reflows at 0.375D and 0.65D, exit at 0.86D. The reflow tweens left/top/width/height in px, so they assume the 1080-wide stage and must be scaled to el; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: layout is tweened via left/top/width/height, forcing layout each frame and assuming a 1080x1920 stage
